title: On /new/ dsh-passwords asks /new/api/dsh-passwords/state (and, with the chat on, /new/gateway/api/messages) under the page's mount, never the bare root (no 404s)
steps: S1: chrome-watch --status (start it with chrome-watch if it is not up). From the repo root at the commit under test, with the stand's dsh built from that commit: node tests/regression/scripts/REG-PR-1085-new-page-passwords-prefix.mjs (TRACY_STAND = the stand's origin, TRACY_STAND_ENV = its .env with SESSION_SECRET).

S2: The script mints a fresh seat (reg-new-prefix-<ms>@example.test, no site), adds its tracy_sess cookie to a new context of the chrome-watch Chrome, opens <stand>/new/ and watches every response for 15 s (REG_WAIT_MS); the internal chat polls /gateway/api/messages every 4 s, but only while it is on.
S3: It records each response whose path ends in /api/dsh-passwords/state or /gateway/api/messages, with its status, and reads chatEnabled from the first state answer that parses.
expect: The script exits 0 and prints 'ALL CHECKS PASSED'.
At least one /api/dsh-passwords/state request is made, and every one is exactly /new/api/dsh-passwords/state answering 200.

Every /gateway/api/messages request (if any) goes under /new/gateway/api/messages and none answers 404; when state says chatEnabled is not false, at least one such request is made. A Tracy seat's state says chatEnabled: false, so the fixed page normally polls none — on the broken page the failed state read left the chat on by default, which is why it also polled /gateway/api/messages at the root.
evidence: tasks/evidence/new-page-passwords-prefix/ — baseline on dsh-passwords 2.7.7-tracy.5 (shared stand tracy.test:8080, read-only page load with a fresh minted seat): three 404 GET /api/dsh-passwords/state and two 404 GET /gateway/api/messages at the bare root, 2 checks failed (baseline-shared-stand-2.7.7-tracy.5.txt); the same 404s on the srd stand before its rebuild (smoke-before-2.7.7-tracy.5).
fence: vendor/tracy/dsh-passwords hook H17: every client /api/… and /gateway/… URL goes through dshUrl() (src/client/tracy/page-base.ts), which resolves it against the page's base href; test/tracy/client-mount.test.ts scans the client for unwrapped literals.
